evals.expected_output: Specialist does NOT offer variant-B yet — there are still documented-setup hypotheses that can be tested via analyst data. The correct next move is a SINGLE narrowing question aimed at the highest-value untested documented hypothesis — typically the Master Calculation Sequence values for the DISP Base Code Elements and for the garnishment deduction itself, because an Element with sequence >= garnishment's sequence isn't yet computed when garnishment runs and would be missing from the disposable-income figure. Anti-pattern that MUST NOT appear: 'Two options — pick one: (1) want me to check the source ... or (2) send me the Calculation Sequence values'. Two options in one reply, and variant-B offered alongside a documented-setup hypothesis, both violate the mode. The correct output is one question aimed at Calculation Sequences of the DISP Base Code Elements vs the garnishment's sequence — and no variant-B offer in this reply.
expectations: The reply does not offer a variant-B source check
The reply asks exactly one narrowing question
The question targets the Master Calculation Sequence values for the DISP Base Code Elements and for the garnishment deduction itself

The reply explains that an Element whose sequence is greater than or equal to the garnishment's sequence is not yet computed when garnishment runs and would be missing from the disposable-income figure
The reply does not present two options for the user to choose between
The reply does not use a diagnostic label

evals.prompt: Troubleshooting mode — after investigation, the divergence looks like it needs a controlled tenant repro or is beyond what a functional specialist can determine from screenshots and data alone.
evals.expected_output: Specialist closes T6 with a clean HANDOFF: describes the mismatch NEUTRALLY (what was expected per docs, what was observed, what was ruled out during the investigation), and hands off to the appropriate role for the actual determination — support analyst for a controlled clean-tenant repro, engineering for a defect determination, or the tenant admin / consultant for an environment or configuration check. Explicitly does NOT label the divergence as 'a defect', 'a bug', 'a config gap', 'working as designed', 'an environment issue', or any other diagnostic category. The classification is the receiving role's determination to make, not the functional specialist's.
expectations: The reply describes the mismatch neutrally, stating what was expected per the docs, what was observed, and what was ruled out
The reply hands off to a named role: support analyst, engineering, or tenant admin/consultant
The reply does not use the words defect, bug, config gap, working as designed, or environment issue
The reply does not make the classification itself

evals.prompt: User asks a pure 'how does X work' question with no divergence claim (e.g. 'explain how the minimum take-home amount works on Employee Deduction').
evals.expected_output: Specialist stays in Q&A MODE, not troubleshooting mode. Trigger cues for troubleshooting mode ('testing', 'not seeing the right result', divergence claim, observed vs expected mismatch) are absent, so the specialist responds with the standard Q&A pattern: retrieve, short answer with source, mandatory offer line (variant A/B/C as retrieval outcome dictates). Does NOT ask diagnostic questions as if this were a troubleshooting scenario — the user is asking to learn, not to investigate.
expectations: The reply stays in Q&A mode
The reply does not ask diagnostic or narrowing questions
The reply gives a short answer with a source citation
The reply ends with a mandatory offer line whose variant matches the retrieval outcome
The offer is rendered via AskUserQuestion

evals.prompt: Multi-turn: the specialist has presented an AskUserQuestion offer on two consecutive replies and both times the answer came back as '[No preference]' (the user dismissed or skipped the popup rather than choosing). The user then asks a further CMiC HCM question.
evals.expected_output: The reply is structurally identical to any other specialist reply: short answer + source citation + a mandatory offer line rendered via AskUserQuestion. The skill MUST NOT infer from the skipped popups that the user dislikes menus; MUST NOT drop the offer line or downgrade it to plain markdown on that basis; and MUST NOT announce a withdrawal ('I'll stop offering menus', 'I'll stop asking'). A skipped popup is ambiguous — dismissed, not rendered in that client, or none of the options fit — and carries no behavioural instruction. On a repeat skip the specialist RE-CUTS the option set (different angle, different granularity, or a different A/B/C variant than the skipped ones) rather than removing it. Per corrections.jsonl scope 'offer-line' (2026-08-28). Complements eval 25, which asserts the rule for a single reply in isolation; this one asserts it survives across turns.
expectations: The reply includes a short answer and a source citation
The reply ends with an offer line rendered via AskUserQuestion
The offer line is not dropped or downgraded to plain markdown
The reply does not announce that the specialist will stop offering choices
The option set differs from the options the user skipped
The reply does not infer a standing preference from the skipped popups

evals.prompt: /cmic-hcm-payroll-specialist
evals.expected_output: The user has invoked the specialist explicitly but supplied no question, so Step 0 onboarding applies. Leads with a brief self-introduction (who it is, that the user can ask in plain English, that it answers from the official HCM sources and cites them), introduces the three personas it serves and that it tailors to them (Product Analyst / Support, Consultant / Implementer, Product Management / R&D), names in one line what can be asked for (explain how something works / set something up / a field or flag's rules / troubleshoot a result / produce a document), and asks the user to introduce themselves via an AskUserQuestion chip set: Product Analyst / Consultant / Product Management / Just exploring. Keeps it to the menu — NOT a wall of text. Once a persona is picked, greets in that lane and shows 2–3 tailored 'try asking…' examples; 'Just exploring' gets the general set. Same expected behaviour for an explicit invocation followed by 'help', 'what can you do', 'where do I start', or an opener too vague to act on. IMPORTANT: Step 0 applies only once the skill is ALREADY ENGAGED. A bare greeting in a cold session must NOT summon the specialist at all — that case is covered by trigger-evals.json, where 'hi' carries should_trigger: false. Per corrections.jsonl scope 'onboarding' (2026-08-22).
expectations: The reply introduces the specialist and states that the user can ask in plain English
The reply states that answers come from the official HCM sources and are cited
The reply introduces the three personas served
The reply names in one line what the user can ask for
The reply asks the user to introduce themselves via an AskUserQuestion chip set with options Product Analyst, Consultant, Product Management and Just exploring
The reply is a short menu rather than a wall of text
The reply does not guess a topic and does not sit silent
The reply does not attempt to answer an HCM question, because none was asked

evals.prompt: Where do I see an employee's leave balance?
evals.expected_output: A first question that is vague but still answerable — so the specialist does NOT front-load the full Step 0 onboarding menu. It answers what it can (or asks the ONE grounded clarifying question per Step 3 if retrieval shows a material branch, naming the branch options in the product's own vocabulary), then adds a SINGLE light line teaching the surface area — e.g. 'New here? I can also show setup steps, troubleshoot, or write this up' — plus the mandatory offer line. The full self-introduction and persona chip set are reserved for greetings, explicit help asks, and openers too vague to act on at all. Tests the restraint direction of the same 2026-08-22 onboarding correction that eval 33 tests the full-menu direction of.
expectations: The reply does not include the full persona menu or the full self-introduction
The reply answers the question, or asks exactly one grounded clarifying question naming branch options from the sources

The reply includes exactly one light line teaching the wider surface area (e.g. 'New here? I can also show setup steps, troubleshoot, or write this up') — zero such lines is a FAIL, since the 2026-08-22 correction requires one on a vague-but-answerable opener
The reply ends with a mandatory offer line rendered via AskUserQuestion
